author: ohtadmin
title: Tour of historic homes Saturday
text:
The annual tour of historic houses will exhibit the Conanicut Park development from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. Saturday, Sept. 20.
Admission on the day of the tour is $25 at 887 East Shore Road via cash or check. Discounted tickets ($20) are available in advance through the “Events” tab at the Jamestown Historical Society’s website.
The development on the north end of Conanicut Island, which was conceived in the 1870s, was inspired by the Methodist camp meeting in Oak Bluffs on Martha’s Vineyard. The plans called for 12 miles of roads, ornamental plantings, a hotel, a commercial area near a wharf, and 2,098 lots to be sold for $150 each. It was “accessible to people who do not keep footmen or carriages, or give champagne breakfasts,” according to Samuel Drake’s 1875 travelogue, “Nooks and Corners of the New England Coast.”
This tour includes three of the original cottages built in 1874 at 883, 887 and 900 East Shore Road. The so-called Chapel House at 887 East Shore, for example, is a 1.5-story Lplan structure. Dubbed a “modest Gothic Revival cottage,” its features include pointed-arch lancet windows, a central entry with drip molding in a three-bay facade with a flat-roofed wraparound piazza supported by plain, square posts.
“It is one of the original Conanicut Park cottages built by Charles Worth of Worth & Brazier,” the brief reads. “Its unique Gothic form reflects the fact that Charles Worth’s base of operations was at Edgartown, on Martha’s Vineyard; this is very much like an Oak Bluffs cottage there. This house was never used as a chapel. Its name was given by Missus Mitchell, who rented it for several years around 1920, because of the long, narrow shape and the treatment of its windows.”
The historical society, which sponsors the event, is asking visitors to consider carpooling. There is no parking on East Shore Road and nearby Court Street, Orient Avenue and Clinton Street only offer parking on one side.
